prompts.grips:
Create an original directional weapon-grip study for the existing top-down 2D wuxia RPG heroes. Reference 1 locks the current male and female design; reference 2 is only a hand-painted ink rendering guide.
Lay out exactly two rows of eight equally scaled full-body figures on clean warm parchment. Top row is the male hero holding the current short sword, bottom row is the female hero holding the current spear with both hands. Directions follow this order: S, SW, W, NW, N, NE, E, SE. Each figure genuinely turns body, face, near/far shoulders, elbows, wrist bends and weapon silhouette to its facing. The sword hand retains a believable one-handed grip, the other arm balances; spear hands stay spaced on one shaft with a believable support grip. Do not mirror east to west. For W/E show true profile face and arm depth; for N/S show correct back/front layering. Keep all eight poses visibly different enough to review.
Zoom enough that shoulder-to-hand anatomy and weapon grips are easy to inspect, while keeping feet and ground pivot visible. Use subtle thin guide marks for pivot, near/far arm and weapon axis, no large UI, no scene background. Show coherent sleeve overlap and weapon depth order.
Original hand-crafted dark-fairytale storybook art: expressive tapered ink contours, restrained hatching, matte watercolor/gouache on aged warm paper, charcoal, muted vermilion, cream and restrained jade. Preserve project identity and cute proportions; do not copy any known game character or asset.
Review study only, not production sprite atlas. No bent arm locked to the same screen side in every facing, no reversed weapon hand, no extra arms/fingers, no cropped body, no text clutter, no glossy anime, no pixel art or photorealism.
prompts.states:
Create an original two-gender action-state key-pose board for the same top-down 2D wuxia RPG, preserving current male/female identity and small chibi proportions from reference 1. Reference 2 guides the dark-fairytale hand-painted ink mood only.
Show ten short horizontal pose strips on warm parchment: male and female versions of channel, dash, hit reaction, death, and respawn. Each strip has four numbered sequential key poses with a small direction arrow and one shared ground line. Channel: gather hands and hold focus, subtle breath, release/cancel settle. Dash: lower center, takeoff, brief low travel pose, foot plant and settle. Hit: body recoil, weapon arm protects grip, controlled recovery without falling instantly. Death: lose balance, drop to knee, land/settle. Respawn: small ink/paper silhouette gathering at ground, rise safely, stand, return to idle. Keep state silhouettes distinct and the movement direction consistent.
Show male/female in paired strips at matched scale, same pose timing and ground pivot, but individual hair and costume motion. Hands, feet, robe tails and weapon should respond to forces. Keep death and respawn non-graphic and readable. Effects are restrained marks, no health UI and no combat result text.
Original matte watercolor and gouache with tapered irregular ink outline, careful hatching, textured paper, earthy charcoal/red-brown/cream/jade palette. Make each pose clean and legible, with generous separation, no borrowed characters or assets from any game.
This is a pose board, not runtime animation. It proposes appearance only and must not suggest changes to gameplay timing, damage, invulnerability or respawn rules. No extra characters, malformed hands, ghost clutter, pixel art, photorealism, shiny 3D or fake text.
prompts.skills:
Create a production-minded visual-effects breakdown sheet for exactly the four existing Cổ skills shown in reference 1. Reference 2 guides the existing skill identity. Preserve their names and shapes: Nguyệt Quang crescent blade, Bạch Ngọc hollow protective ward, Bạch Hạc low feather dash, Băng Tằm angular frost silk and crystals.
Use four horizontal rows with equal columns for four moments: icon/symbol, cast, travel or guard hold, impact/end. Each effect must have one large clear silhouette, plus a small 48px icon preview and a separate 32px icon check. Preserve negative space around the tiny hero. Make layer intent visually clear: ink contour, colored body, sparse paper fleck/brush edge, timing fade. Do not cover the player or obscure the ground direction. Nguyệt Quang is a single sharp crescent; Bạch Ngọc stays hollow so the hero is visible inside; Bạch Hạc is a low ground-hugging feather arc; Băng Tằm uses thin silk lines and a few angular crystals.
Follow an original hand-painted dark-fairytale game style with tapered ink, selective hatching, matte watercolor/gouache, subdued cream, jade, slate-blue and charcoal accents on warm paper. No neon, bloom, generic magic circles, particle clouds or borrowed game art.
Keep cast, travel/hold, impact and fade visually distinguishable but tightly controlled for readability in actual play. Icons remain identifiable in monochrome and at small size. This is a visual recipe board only; it does not set balance, range, duration, damage, status, cooldown or input behavior. Do not add extra skills, numbers or fake text.
